content.title: Go out of this world with NASA - App Store
content.text: Becoming an astronaut is… a challenge. So, if you can’t see yourself going beyond the stratosphere in person, here’s your chance to live vicariously through the experiences of NASA’s team and technologies.The app is a hub of incredible high-res images and videos of space, updates on missions and information on satellites, rovers and telescopes.Here are five out-of-this-world discoveries to make with the app.The next blast-off Check out the Launch Schedule for details of NASA’s upcoming missions. Turn on notifications for NASA Events and the app will let you know when something big is happening. Check the Launch Schedule to see what’s coming up from NASA and other space agencies.You’ll find dates for your diary, including rover landings, Space Station resupply missions and brand-new exploration missions.The position of planets Find out more about Saturn – including how it compares to Earth. Real-time data is used to map out the solar system, so you can see how everything lines up using the NASA app. For example, zoom in on Saturn and you can find out the current position of the gas giant’s nine largest moons (and that it has 82 moons in total).Check out each planet’s fact pages for even more detail, including their stats relative to Earth.A planet you’ve never heard of Learn about oval-shaped planet Haumea (no, we hadn’t heard of it either). What do you know about Haumea, the oval-shaped dwarf planet beyond the orbit of Neptune? Ever heard of Makemake? How about the hypothetical Planet X (also known – confusingly – as Planet Nine) for which new clues have recently been uncovered?You’ll find information about all of these within the Planets section of the app.When the ISS will pass you Discover when you might be able to spot the International Space Station. Give the app access to your location data and it can send you notifications for possible sightings of the International Space Station (ISS).Check out the Sightings section (where you can also track the Hubble telescope and Landsat and Terra satellites) and tap on Sky View to see a countdown to the next passing.What NASA is up to right now Read the latest news from NASA and watch live broadcasts from space. In the TV and Audio area you can tune into NASA TV Media for live broadcasts from space to see what the astronauts are up to (yep, they are being interviewed while floating around the Space Station).You can also read the latest news articles from NASA and listen to the official podcast – Houston, we have a podcast!
